lines.trans: Where is Samsonov? He is not answering his phone.
I do not know. He did not spend the night at home.
We have the debate tomorrow!
I know. I am very worried about him.
He is completely unprepared.
Vanya is very upset because of the rumors.
The rumors about his grandfather are Osipenko's provocation.
But people believe this lie.
We must win this election!
Without Vanya we will do nothing.
We need to find him urgently!
Where are we going to look for him?
Check all the bars and old friends.
I will call acquaintances right now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: 'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
Go on, tell her. Nina doesn't believe it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.

examples.trans: He is running in the election.

examples.text: У меня много дел. Выборы мэра…
examples.trans: I've got a lot to do. The mayoral election...

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Паша, эти выборы ты не выиграешь.
examples.trans: Pasha, you won't win this election.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

examples.text: Посмотрим, придёт ли этот кандидат на дебаты!
examples.trans: We will see whether this candidate comes to the debate!
Televised debates will take place in the evening.

meanings.note: masculine noun that declines like a feminine -а noun

examples.text: Значит, надо глубже копать! Дальние родственники, дедушки и бабушки.
examples.trans: That means we have to dig deeper! Distant relatives, grandfathers and grandmothers.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.
The main thing is, you keep him at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: short forms знаком, знакома, знакомо, знакомы (+ dative)

examples.text: А знакомо ли тебе, Аркашка, слово педикюр?
examples.trans: And are you familiar, Arkashka, with the word pedicure?

examples.text: Я услышал в коридоре знакомый голос.
examples.trans: I heard a familiar voice in the corridor.
I will call acquaintances right now.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'lie, falsehood' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a real lie detector, Fedya.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: to spend the night, stay overnight
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to spend the night'.

examples.trans: He did not spend the night at home.

examples.text: Я не знаю. Он не ночевал дома.
examples.trans: I do not know. He did not spend the night at home.

examples.text: Ты ночуешь в ресторане шефа Баринова?!
examples.trans: You spend the night in Chef Barinov's restaurant?!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

переживать.gloss: to worry, to fret; to go through

examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Что вы так переживаете? Самсонов всё, он себя закопал.
examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that? Samsonov is finished, he buried himself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'готовить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to get ready', paired with 'подготавливать'.

examples.text: Мы всё подготовили и прилетели на сделку.
examples.trans: We got everything ready and flew in for the deal.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'provocation' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'rumor, hearing' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vanya is very upset because of the rumors.

examples.text: Слухи про дедушку — это провокация Осипенко.
examples.trans: The rumors about his grandfather are Osipenko's provocation.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

examples.text: Славик, смотри сюда. Меняю свой новый айфон на твой старый телефон.
examples.trans: Slavik, look here. I'll swap my new iPhone for your old phone.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
